subtopic: Responding to a natural disaster or accident
subtype: Approach: freezing or denying the danger [Pitfall]
passage: The floor gave a small shudder during English, and Salma didn't look up from her phone. Probably a truck, she thought, and scrolled on. Then the windows rattled and Ms D'Souza shouted, “Under the desks, now!” All around her chairs scraped and bags dropped. Salma's mind went blank. Which way was she supposed to go? Nobody had ever made them practise, and now nothing came. Maria grabbed her wrist and pulled her down beside her, and Salma banged her elbow on the desk leg. Dust drifted from the ceiling. When it stopped, her hands were cold and the elbow throbbed. “I just sat there,” she whispered. Ms D'Souza said later that the class would rehearse the drill properly, and Salma kept thinking about the seconds she had lost.

qa.q: What did Salma bang her elbow on?
qa.a: Salma banged her elbow on the desk leg.

qa.q: What was Salma thinking when the floor first shuddered?
qa.a: She thought it was probably a truck, so she felt no alarm and kept scrolling on her phone.

qa.q: What could the class and Salma do so the next tremor goes better?
qa.a: The class could rehearse the drill until the steps come automatically, and Salma could put her phone down and look up at the very first shake.

qa.q: How might Maria have seen Salma freeze?
qa.a: Maria probably felt alarmed and urgent, and acted fast by pulling Salma down beside her, while worrying about Salma. 😔

grounding: At the first tremor a teen keeps scrolling, thinking it is nothing, and loses seconds because no rehearsed action comes to mind.

passage:
Dear Charu,
You asked if we felt the earthquake in Guwahati. We did. And I did everything wrong.
I was on my bed scrolling when it started to shake. I actually thought, it's a truck passing, and kept watching the video. Then the ceiling fan swung and the glass on my table fell. Even then I just sat there with the phone in my hand. My head was completely blank. We'd never practised anything at home, and all I could think was, what do I do?
Ma screamed my name from the corridor. By the time I moved, the shaking was nearly over. The bookshelf beside my bed had tipped over onto the mattress where my legs had been a second before.
Nobody was hurt. But I lost maybe fifteen seconds just staring.
This weekend Ma and I are making a plan and practising it. Want me to send it to you?
Jaya

qa.q: What did Jaya first think the shaking was?
What was Jaya feeling as the fan swung?
qa.a: Jaya felt frozen and confused, mind completely blank, with no practised action to fall back on.

qa.q: What could Jaya's family do before another tremor?
qa.a: Agree on and practise what to do, such as taking cover under a sturdy table away from shelves, so the body knows the steps.

qa.q: How might Ma have felt screaming Jaya's name from the corridor?
qa.a: Ma was probably terrified, and later shaken to see the bookshelf on the mattress where Jaya had been.

grounding: Shows a teen who keeps scrolling at the first tremor, thinking it is nothing, and loses precious seconds because no action had ever been rehearsed.

passage:
Rajni, you asked why I'm so strict about our earthquake drill now. I'm Urmila, and it's because of Dharamshala, last March.
We were in the hostel study room. The table began to tremble and a pen rolled off. Everyone looked up, and I looked back down at my phone. I honestly thought, that's nothing, someone's jumping upstairs. I kept scrolling. Then the windows rattled, and the girl next to me was already under the table, and I was still sitting there holding the phone, with no idea what to do. Not a single step came into my head. We'd never practised in that building.
It stopped after maybe twenty seconds. The big wall clock came down right behind my chair.
Nothing happened to me. But I wasted those seconds. So now, when the warden calls a drill, I'm first under the table, and I make you do it too.

qa.q: What came down behind Urmila's chair?
What did Urmila feel when the windows rattled?
qa.a: Urmila felt frozen and lost, holding the phone with no idea what to do.

qa.q: What habit did Urmila build afterwards, and why does it help?
qa.a: Being first under the table in every drill, so a practised step comes to mind instantly instead of a blank.

qa.q: How might the girl under the table have seen Urmila?
qa.a: The girl might have been alarmed to see Urmila still sitting there with the phone, unsure whether to call out.

grounding: Shows a teen who keeps scrolling at the first tremor, thinking it is nothing, and loses precious seconds because nothing had ever been rehearsed.
